column1: # rank.exe refute -- one row per (target, colour)
# mined: 1 = the miner found a win, 0 = conceded
# verify: W/L/D for the BOOK's side, replayed through openerBook by the wearer
# blocked_shared: every position on the losing line was owned by an already-won
#   line, so no move could be changed without breaking one. That is the merge
#   conflict a single position-keyed book cannot express.
# audit: 1 = the WRITTEN book won this line replayed on its own. Distinct from
#   `mined`, which only says the line was found while our side was still
# oob_first: the first of OUR moves the book did not serve, so the fallback brain
#   had to choose (-1 = the book covered the whole line). A line with oob_first
#   >= 0 was carried by the brain, not by the book, whatever its result says.
# v_plies: half-moves in the openerBook verification game. A line that matches
#   `plies` played the same length game the miner recorded.
